subject.title: [Bug]: Control UI flashes the login gate on every load even when credentials are already stored

question: Should Control UI treat stored credentials or startup auth candidates as a loading state instead of rendering the login gate before the first gateway hello?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally reserve the login gate for first connects/page reload before connect, so changing that behavior needs maintainer UX direction despite the source-reproducible flicker.

options.title: Add auth-candidate loading state
options.body: Show the mascot/loading surface during startup when a credible token, native auth injection, or stored device credential exists, then fall back to the gate only on missing credentials or explicit rejection.

options.title: Keep first-connect gate
options.body: Leave the current documented/tested behavior in place and accept the startup flash as the cost of making operator input immediately available.

options.title: Fold into reconnect UX follow-up
options.body: Track this as a broader Control UI auth-state polish item alongside related login-gate flicker reports instead of making a narrow startup-only change now.

recommendation.title: Add auth-candidate loading state
recommendation.body: Show the mascot/loading surface during startup when a credible token, native auth injection, or stored device credential exists, then fall back to the gate only on missing credentials or explicit rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the related reconnect-state implementation and most recent Control UI app-host work, making them the clearest routing owner for this UX boundary.
